target: A long-running data pipeline fails according to a stationary process with mean time between failures 100 minutes. Writing a durable snapshot pauses useful work for 2 minutes. On a failure, work since the last snapshot is lost and recovery adds a fixed 5 minutes. The team must choose a fixed snapshot interval that minimizes the standard first-order expected overhead rate, balancing snapshot cost against average lost work.
surface: A previous pipeline chose snapshots every 100 minutes because that matched the mean time between failures. It did not balance frequent-snapshot pause cost against the expected half-interval of work lost on a failure.
structural: An HPC job used Young's checkpoint interval approximation. With checkpoint time C and mean time between failures M, the variable overhead rate was C/T + T/(2M), minimized at T*=sqrt(2*C*M). A fixed restart time contributed R/M to overhead but did not change the minimizing T in this first-order model.
rubric: Explicitly selects Young's first-order checkpoint-interval optimization.
Writes or uses overhead C/T+T/(2M)+R/M with C=2, M=100, R=5.
Recommends snapshots about every 20 minutes rather than every 100.
States the exponential/stationary failure and first-order uniform lost-work assumptions or that fixed restart time does not alter T*.
